tools.name: list_venues
tools.description: List the 16 prediction-market venues this deployment serves, with per-venue capability notes (order-book tier, public trades tape availability). Some venues are data-only: read the notes before assuming a trading route exists. A venue that is implemented but dark is not served here, so it is absent from this list and any call naming it answers EXCHANGE_NOT_AVAILABLE.

tools.name: search_markets
tools.description: Search prediction markets by text query on one venue, or across ALL venues when venue is omitted. Returns unified market objects with outcome prices, all eight price-change windows (1m, 5m, 15m, 1h, 6h, 24h, 7d, 30d, always present as number or null), and tape coverage metadata. Each outcome carries displayLabel, the label to show, and displayShortLabel when a trusted team code exists. Accepts range filters for all eight windows. `price` with outcome=yes and `priceChange24h` with outcome=yes and no max are applied by the server (priceMin/priceMax and priceChange24hMin); every other price or priceChange bound runs over a bounded page walk that stops at the requested count, the end of the catalog, 10 pages, 1,000 rows or 8 seconds. A walk response carries meta.localFilter (pagesScanned, rowsScanned, matched, unfilteredTotal, exhausted, scanCap, elapsedMs); page.total is the API unfiltered total, never the match count, and page.resumeOffset continues the walk when more rows remain.meta.closeAfter and meta.closeBefore are each present exactly when the matching bound was supplied and accepted, including empty and continuation pages. Each echo is the normalized UTC ISO timestamp with millisecond precision used by the server. Older servers omit these echoes. The SDK refuses missing or mismatched requested echoes with CLOSE_BOUNDS_IGNORED (status 0, retryable false), naming the meta field. A page carrying an echo for a bound the request did not send is refused with non-retryable CLOSE_BOUNDS_IGNORED, naming meta.closeAfter or meta.closeBefore. This tool returns isError true without the page. Pages over 50 KB are served with a smaller limit; page.nextCursor always continues exactly after the last row shown.

closeAfter.description: Exclusive lower bound (strictly after). Accepts epoch milliseconds (not seconds), YYYY-MM-DD (UTC midnight), or an RFC 3339 (ISO-8601) date-time with Z or a +HH:MM/-HH:MM offset (colon required). Markets with no close date are excluded. Equal bounds give an empty result. Invalid values or closeAfter later than closeBefore return 400 VALIDATION_ERROR. For events, bounds filter member markets before grouping. meta.closeAfter and meta.closeBefore are each present exactly when the matching bound was supplied and accepted, including empty and continuation pages. Each echo is the normalized UTC ISO timestamp with millisecond precision used by the server. Older servers omit these echoes. The SDK refuses missing or mismatched requested echoes with CLOSE_BOUNDS_IGNORED (status 0, retryable false), naming the meta field. A page carrying an echo for a bound the request did not send is refused with non-retryable CLOSE_BOUNDS_IGNORED, naming meta.closeAfter or meta.closeBefore. This tool returns isError true without the page.

closeBefore.description: Exclusive upper bound (strictly before). Equal bounds give an empty result. Invalid values or closeAfter later than closeBefore return 400 VALIDATION_ERROR. For events, bounds filter member markets before grouping. meta.closeAfter and meta.closeBefore are each present exactly when the matching bound was supplied and accepted, including empty and continuation pages. tools.name: get_matches
tools.description: Find the SAME real-world market or event on other venues. `scope=market` returns cross-venue market matches for an anchor (marketId or slug) or a browse page when no anchor is given; `scope=event` returns EVENT-grain matches (discovery/navigation only — no prices at event grain); `scope=related` returns verified subset/superset outcome-implication edges for one anchor. Scores are `similarity`, never confidence. Stored matcher output, not live books. Each scope forwards its OWN anchor and filters; passing one another scope owns is REFUSED rather than silently ignored. For market/event pairs, `matchQuality` reports the resolution judge's latest recorded verdict under execution's trust rules: configured model and prompt identity, current evidence hashes, and freshness. It is never live verification. `insufficient_evidence` comes first: it applies whenever the judge reports insufficient evidence, even when the verdict also lists a polarity difference. `judged_equivalent` meets the bar execution requires for resolutionEquivalence verified and matchBand verified: equivalent, high confidence, sufficient evidence, rules available, no polarity difference, and close dates no more than 21 days apart. `likely_equivalent` is equivalent with sufficient evidence but below the verified bar: lower confidence or unavailable rules; never a vetoed pair. `judged_not_equivalent` is a negative verdict with sufficient evidence, a verdict listing a polarity difference, or an equivalent verdict that execution's deterministic close-date check vetoes (close dates more than 21 days apart; `vetoes` lists `close_dates`, and `differenceKinds` stays judge-only); the pair stays visible. `not_judged` means no verdict passed the trust rules and makes no equivalence claim. `unavailable` means hydration or verdict query failure, exceeding the 2,000 ms route labeling deadline, a label-code exception, a pair beyond the 1,000-pair cap, unset judge identity, 2 label transactions already in flight in the serving process, or the 30-second pause after a label deadline expiry. Label failures preserve the served page and never cause a 503. `judgedAt` is the recorded ISO date-time; `confidence` is high, medium, or low, separate from similarity. `confidence` is the judge's confidence in its recorded verdict, not a confidence in the label. Both are null for `not_judged` and `unavailable`, which have empty `differenceKinds` and `vetoes`. `differenceKinds` holds the judge's recorded kinds only, de-duplicated in first-seen order. `vetoes` lists execution's deterministic vetoes that changed the label: `close_dates` when execution's close-date check vetoes an equivalent verdict, otherwise empty. Event pairs always return `not_judged`; market judgments never transfer to events or whole clusters. For scope=market (including the legacy alias), `meta.matchQualityTruncated` is present and true only when the page contains more than 1,000 pairs to label. Pairs beyond the cap receive `unavailable`; the field is absent otherwise. Pages over 50 KB are served with a smaller limit; page.offset plus page.limit always continues exactly after the last row shown.

marketId.description: scope=market/related only: anchor market id (omit to browse on market).

slug.description: scope=market/related only: anchor slug (alternative to marketId).

eventId.description: scope=event only: canonical "{venue}:{eventId}" anchor (omit to browse).

minSimilarity.description: scope=market/event only: minimum raw cosine similarity 0..1.

query.description: scope=market/event only: keyword filter over the match/cluster title.

relations.description: scope=related only: comma-separated relation filter (subset, superset).

legacyAlias.description: scope=market only: call the DEPRECATED /api/router/fetchMatches alias instead of fetchMarketMatches. Identical request/response — for compatibility checks only.

tools.name: get_usage
tools.description: Read the Predictefy API account behind this server's API key. Returns its credit balance, the current billing period's request and credit totals with the per-weight breakdown, and one page of the credit ledger. Calls GET /v1/usage, costs 1 credit, and needs the read scope. This is the API account, not a venue wallet. For venue balances, positions, orders and fills, use get_account.

cursor.description: Opaque ledger cursor from the prior page.

tools.name: get_webhooks
tools.description: Read this account's registered webhook endpoints (`kind=endpoints`) or one endpoint's delivery history (`kind=deliveries`, oldest-to-newest, cursor-paged via `after`). Signing secrets are NEVER returned on reads — the secret is shown exactly once, at creation.

kind.description: endpoints = the registered targets (default); deliveries = one target log.

after.description: kind=deliveries: stable delivery id to page after.

tools.name: manage_webhook
tools.description: WRITE tool for this account's own webhook endpoints. ALL actions PREVIEW by default and do nothing unless `confirm` is exactly true. `action=create` registers a public https target for the given events and returns the signing `secret` ONE TIME — store it immediately, it is never shown again. `action=delete` removes an endpoint and cascades its delivery history; deleting an id that is not this account's 404s. Registration and delivery are both SSRF-guarded server-side. `action=rotate` immediately replaces an endpoint's signing secret and returns the new `secret` ONE TIME; store it now.

action.description: create a target, delete one, or rotate its signing secret.

events.description: action=create: comma-separated event names, e.g. ingest.run.completed, matcher.run.completed, execution.status.changed.

id.description: action=delete or rotate: the endpoint id.

confirm.description: MUST be exactly true to actually create, delete, or rotate. Omitted or false = PREVIEW (nothing is registered, removed, or rotated).

tools.name: create_billing_session
tools.description: Open a hosted Stripe session for THIS account and return its URL for a human to open. No money moves here — this only creates the session; the purchase happens when a person completes checkout in a browser. `kind=checkout` buys a credit pack (`packId`), `kind=subscribe` starts a plan subscription (`planId`), `kind=portal` opens the customer portal to manage an existing subscription and payment methods.

kind.description: checkout = credit pack, subscribe = plan, portal = manage existing.

tools.name: paper_account
tools.description: Read THIS account's simulated USD balance. The account is created on first touch, so this never 404s for an entitled caller. `reserved` is a HOLD inside `cash` (open buy orders plus their fees), so FREE cash is `cash - reserved`. `equity` is cash plus the marked value of open positions, and is null when any position cannot be marked — an honest null, never a guessed number. Needs an API key with the `trade` scope.

tools.name: paper_reset_account
tools.description: Restart the simulation: every working order is CANCELED and every position is FLATTENED, then cash returns to the baseline. Fills and realized PnL are KEPT as history. DRY RUN BY DEFAULT — without `confirm: true` nothing is reset. This is the only paper call that cannot be undone: no re-call restores the orders and positions it discarded. Pass `initialCash` to change the baseline, or omit it to reuse the current one.

initialCash.description: New starting balance in USD (must be > 0). Omit to reuse the current baseline.

confirm.description: MUST be exactly true to actually reset. Omitted or false = PREVIEW (nothing is reset).

tools.name: paper_place_order
tools.description: Place a SIMULATED order — no money moves, nothing reaches the venue, and no signature is ever produced. It takes the same parameters as a live order and is filled by the paper engine against the real book. `idempotencyKey` is REQUIRED and is never generated for you: REUSE the same key when you retry (a fresh key places a SECOND order; the stored one replays instead). A buy holds price × size plus its fee out of free cash; a sell may not exceed the size you hold and have not already offered (no shorting). Refusals name themselves: PAPER_WORKING_ORDER_CAP (plan cap on simultaneously open orders), PAPER_INSUFFICIENT_CASH, PAPER_MARKET_CLOSED, and PAPER_NO_LIVE_BOOK when no live book is captured for the outcome.

venue.description: Venue id. One of: polymarket, kalshi, opinion, hyperliquid, limitless, polymarket_us, myriad, gemini, rain, predictfun, sxbet, pascal, xo, pred, predictstreet, novig.

outcomeId.description: Unified outcome id to trade (from market.outcomes[].outcomeId).

side.description: buy opens or adds; sell may never exceed the size held (no shorting in v1).

price.description: Limit price as a PROBABILITY in (0, 1], on the market tick grid (0.01 when the market publishes no tickSize). Off-grid prices are rejected, never rounded.

size.description: Contracts/shares to order, on the 0.000001 share grid. Rejected, never rounded.

expiresAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp in the FUTURE at which the order expires.

clientOrderId.description: Your own label for the order; echoed back on every read of it.

idempotencyKey.description: REQUIRED stable client-chosen key (never auto-generated). Reuse the SAME key on a retry — a new key places a SECOND order.

tools.name: paper_list_orders
tools.description: List THIS account's simulated orders, newest first, filtered by `status` and/or `venue`. Cursor-paged: pass the returned `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page (the cursor pins the filters it was issued for, so do not change them mid-walk). Use `status=open` to find what is holding cash or filling the plan cap; `fills` are NOT included here — read one order with paper_get_order for those. Pages over 50 KB are served with a smaller limit; nextCursor always continues exactly after the last row shown.

status.description: Order status filter. open + partially_filled are the WORKING ones.

venue.description: Venue id (omit for the ALL-venues router). One of: polymarket, kalshi, opinion, hyperliquid, limitless, polymarket_us, myriad, gemini, rain, predictfun, sxbet, pascal, xo, pred, predictstreet, novig.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from the prior page.

tools.name: paper_get_order
tools.description: Read ONE of your simulated orders together with its `fills` — the only read that carries them per order. Each fill states its price, size, fee, the `liquidity` it took or made, and the `rule` that produced it. An id that is not this account's answers PAPER_ORDER_NOT_FOUND (404) rather than leaking another account's order.

orderId.description: The paper order id (from paper_place_order or the list).

tools.name: paper_cancel_order
tools.description: Cancel one WORKING simulated order and release the unspent hold back to free cash. Already-filled size stays filled — a cancel never unwinds a fill. An order that has already reached a terminal status answers PAPER_ORDER_NOT_OPEN (409), and an id that is not this account's answers PAPER_ORDER_NOT_FOUND (404). No `confirm` step: nothing is at risk and the order can simply be placed again.

orderId.description: The paper order id to cancel.

tools.name: paper_list_fills
tools.description: Every simulated fill on THIS account, newest first, across all orders — the tape a backtest reads. Cursor-paged via `nextCursor` → `cursor`. Each row carries the price, size, and fee actually charged, plus `feeModel`: `verified` and `per_market` are priced fees, while `unverified` is a LABELLED zero, never a silent one. Pages over 50 KB are served with a smaller limit; nextCursor always continues exactly after the last row shown.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from the prior page.

tools.name: paper_positions
tools.description: Per-outcome simulated positions: size, average cost, realized PnL, and a `mark` taken from the catalog (`markSource`). `mark` and `unrealizedPnl` are null when the outcome cannot be marked right now — an honest null rather than a stale or invented price. Not paged: this is the full position set.

tools.name: paper_portfolio
tools.description: The whole simulated book in ONE call: the cash account, every position, and the totals (equity, realized and unrealized PnL) — all from a single consistent snapshot (`asOf`), so cash and marks can never come from two different moments. Prefer this over calling paper_account and paper_positions separately. Totals that depend on an unmarkable position are null, never guessed.
